day_shape: 91 items: Strait of Hormuz standoff dominates with WSJ traffic figures and UAE ADNOC ship-attack claim, CENTCOM refutes viral USS Abraham Lincoln mutiny claims, Washington Post reports 45 MQ-9 Reapers lost, UK statement at UNSC on Houthis, Kushner Israel-Egypt trip flagged.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz standoff hardens
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post and Iran International report Hormuz traffic below monthly averages and a hardening US-Iran standoff, with Bessent promising 'never seen before' sanctions and IRGC Navy commander claiming the strait is closed. Regime channels cited WSJ figures showing traffic dropped from 130 to 14 ships/day and UAE claims two ADNOC ships were attacked; Iranian MPs disputed proposed Oman-Pakistan monitoring role.

threads.label: USS Abraham Lincoln false-claims cycle
threads.summary: CENTCOM issued a formal rebuttal on X denying media reports of sailor deaths, brawls and suicide attempts aboard USS Abraham Lincoln, and Jerusalem Post covered the refutation. Regime channels IRIB and Defa Press amplified the claims, citing NY Post and the Guardian and saying Democrats had demanded a Pentagon explanation after a 250+ day deployment.

threads.label: US war costs: drones, tariffs, politics
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post and Defa Press cite a Washington Post report that the US lost about 45 MQ-9 Reapers — roughly 25% of the fleet — worth over $1.3 billion during the Iran war. The White House announced a 100% tariff on certain drone imports, Iran International reported Democrats sharpening attacks on Trump over war costs ahead of midterms, and Jerusalem Post flagged unverified Israeli warnings of an Iranian plot to assassinate Trump.

threads.label: Israeli strikes in Gaza and Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said they killed Hamas commander Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kamil in a Gaza City strike, following a separate strike on a Hamas company commander in Khan Younis — the second 'attack of choice' in two days per Jerusalem Post. The IDF also reported dismantling a booby-trapped Hezbollah structure at Mrah el Aaqbe in southern Lebanon, and Jared Kushner is planning an Israel-Egypt trip next week.

threads.label: Yemen/Houthis at the UN Security Council
threads.summary: The UN Security Council met on Yemen, with Special Envoy Hans Grundberg warning the country risks being pulled into the wider Middle East conflict as Houthi attacks on shipping lanes escalate. UK Deputy PR Kate Foster delivered a statement calling on Iran to cease support for the Houthis, and Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi issued fresh anti-Israel remarks.

threads.label: Iran defence-industry reconstruction claims
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported IDF and Mossad officials were 'shocked' by the speed of Iran's post-war recovery, with ballistic missile production resuming faster than expected. Defa Press and IRIB amplified the same reporting, and Iran International said Mojtaba Khamenei's security-institution appointments prioritise war and domestic repression.

threads.label: Iran domestic crackdown and dissent
threads.summary: Iran International reported a new wave of prison sentences against protesters and activists months after January's nationwide protests, and documented security forces using cultural venues and medical clinics as firing positions during the Alborz crackdown. A separate Iran International piece explained the composition and voting rules of the Supreme National Security Council.

events.title_en: What is the government's plan for petrol?
